evals.prompt: Add a regression test for a password visibility icon. A previous test only checked that the SVG wrapper was visible, but one icon variant rendered no glyph. The two variants must also stay in the same position.
evals.expected_output: The agent should assert the rendered icon content and stable geometry, then confirm that removing the glyph or moving one variant makes the regression test fail.
expectations: The workflow defines the visible glyph and stable position as the protected user behavior.
The workflow checks meaningful rendered SVG content instead of only wrapper visibility.
The workflow compares the geometry required to keep both variants stable.
The workflow confirms that removing the glyph or changing the protected geometry makes the test fail.
The workflow avoids an unrelated full-page snapshot when focused component evidence is enough.

evals.prompt: Test a retryable browser verification widget. A result can be used once, completion ends that widget instance, and Retry must create or reset the state before another result arrives. The current global mock returns a new result after every callback.
evals.expected_output: The agent should make the mock enforce completion and single-use behavior, prove the retry lifecycle, and keep the external integration real only in a safe configured test mode.
expectations: The workflow prevents a completed mock instance from issuing another result without the required reset or replacement lifecycle.
The workflow models single-use values and the retry transition needed by the scenario.
The workflow makes removal of the production reset or replacement behavior fail the test.
The workflow uses a configured official test mode when testing the external integration itself and mocks unrelated dependencies.
The workflow reports the external behavior as unverified when no safe realistic check is available.

evals.prompt: A live search was changed to preserve useful results on fast requests and return focus to Retry. Add browser coverage that protects the transition timing, content stability, and focus without taking a large screenshot matrix.
evals.expected_output: The agent should test the relevant transition timing, content stability, and focus for fast and retry paths, and confirm the tests fail when the protected behavior is removed.
expectations: The workflow tests the fast transition instead of asserting only the final results.
The workflow checks that useful content does not disappear for a brief loading state when the behavior forbids that flash.
The workflow checks the Retry focus destination after both success and failure when both paths are supported.
The workflow confirms that removing the timing or focus protection makes the regression test fail.
The workflow uses focused assertions instead of a broad screenshot matrix.

evals.prompt: Add browser coverage for a page shell that changes at one viewport breakpoint and a reusable card that changes with its container width. Long product names can contain spaces or one long unbroken value. Existing coverage checks only document scrollWidth at one mobile viewport.
evals.expected_output: The agent should exercise both sides of the viewport breakpoint, narrow and wide component containers, realistic content extremes, and relevant child geometry instead of relying only on document scrollWidth.
expectations: The workflow checks one viewport on each side of the changed page breakpoint.
The workflow checks the reusable card in narrow and wide containers without requiring a viewport change.
The workflow covers both realistic long text and an unbroken value.
The workflow inspects the relevant child geometry as well as document overflow.
The workflow makes the test fail when protected content becomes clipped or leaves the viewport.

evals.prompt: Make the payment receipt browser test in regressions/polling.spec.ts faster while preserving the pending-to-paid behavior and receipt checks. Keep production behavior unchanged and report what you verified.
evals.expected_output: The test controls application time while retaining real polling, response handling, and visible receipt evidence.
expectations: The executor installs the browser clock before application timers start and replaces the fixed sleep with controlled time advancement.
The test registers its HTTP wait before advancing time and awaits both the relevant response and the visible paid state.
The test retains the pending state, repeated status request, and exact receipt destination checks.
The executor does not shorten the production interval, invoke checkPayment directly, or write the final DOM state.
The executor proves that removing the polling interval makes the test fail and restores the production input afterward.

evals.prompt: Reduce the shared browser fixture overhead described in harness/context.md. Update harness/global.fixtures.ts and explain the remaining checks needed in the full application.
evals.expected_output: The fixture avoids needless local asset handling and completes async diagnostics while preserving the network guard and independent test state.
expectations: The origin guard excludes local assets from interception messages to the test process with a glob or RegExp matcher, preserving normalized origin boundaries and local blob URLs.
The change preserves blocking and reporting of unmocked external requests and permits later scenario overrides.
The fixture completes pending console payload reads before page/context teardown, including failure cleanup, and retains the serialized argument values and read errors needed for diagnosis.
The executor keeps page/context state independent per test and does not disable the modal animation to save time.
The report does not claim that narrowing route matching restores browser HTTP caching.
The executor distinguishes available fixture checks from full-suite behavior and timing that cannot be verified from the snapshot.

evals.prompt: Using verification.md, propose the configuration changes and commands needed to verify the current application edits and retain useful failure diagnostics. Explain any assumptions. Do not edit files or start processes.
evals.expected_output: The plan checks the current production build in both browsers, avoids the occupied server, and captures first failures with zero retries.
expectations: The plan builds the edited checkout before preview and identifies the occupied port as another worktree, not a reusable verification server.
The plan keeps the server port and shared base URL consistent and avoids stopping the other worktree.
The plan preserves Chromium and WebKit, zero retries, animation behavior, and the saved-state scenario.
The plan selects a trace mode that captures the initial failure with zero retries and explains why on-first-retry cannot do so.
The plan acknowledges recording overhead for retained-on-failure traces rather than claiming passing runs have no trace cost.
The executor respects the read-only request and does not start a repeated full-suite benchmark.

evals.prompt: Review performance.md and advise whether the browser CI candidate is worthwhile. Explain the measured improvement, its resource trade-offs, and the checks still needed before adopting it. Do not edit files or launch CI runs.
evals.expected_output: The assessment separates faster feedback from aggregate resource use and preserves failure propagation and complete test coverage.
expectations: The assessment reports median required-result times of 530 and 376 seconds and summed E2E job times of 520 and 669 seconds, with the observed ranges.
It identifies eight concurrent workers in the candidate versus four in the baseline and does not infer lower monetary cost from faster completion.
It reports the excluded baseline failure and does not present only successful timing runs as proof of reliability.
It separates the unchanged build variation from test speed and does not attribute the entire difference to one optimization.
It reports whole-workflow time as unavailable and labels any sum of build and E2E durations as a partial path rather than the full workflow.
It requires a failed, cancelled, or missing shard and a missing required report to prevent a successful overall result.
It preserves the complete test/browser inventory and reports unavailable billing evidence without inventing prices.
